title: Grateful Dead Live at Piedmont Park on 1969-07-07
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with some hiss and early‑stage feedback, yet captures a high‑energy 1969 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star and a monster Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The audience‑sourced soundboard tape is raw – noticeable hiss and a brief bout of feedback in the opening minutes – but it remains clear enough to enjoy. Musically the concert erupts after a shaky start, delivering an incendiary Dark Star, a soaring Eleven, and arguably the best Lovelight of the era, with Pigpen driving the crowd and Jerry’s guitar soaring. Overall the performance is energetic and memorable despite a few rough early numbers.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars, praising the show’s energy and standout jams while noting only minor recording flaws; this consensus yields a strong positive rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Raw tape with noticeable hiss and early‑set feedback, but overall clear and listenable; occasional roughness in the first four songs does not detract from the main performance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The first few songs are a bit rough, but the band quickly gains momentum; the second set builds into extended jams that drive the concert to a high‑energy climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is praised (especially in Lovelight) and he provides strong backing vocals on Mama Tried, though his early‑set vocals are noted as rough.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s stage antics, off‑key shouts, and crowd‑working during Lovelight are highlighted; also mentioned hobbling with a cast earlier in the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ contributions shine on the Eleven and add texture throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum intro to Lovelight is described as groovy and syncopated, with tight playing overall.
